scope: 125 formula trials published 2015–2020 in Helfer et al. detailed evaluation
denominator_type: trial reports as defined by review

groups.name: Funding reported; industry support not reported

additional.label: Industry statistical analysis or writing when role clearly described

quick: Companies supported many of these trials. That is a reason to check independent evidence for extra product benefits, not to avoid safe formula.
limitations: Funding and risk-of-bias categories are separate; not all formula research. Review correction n2890 supplied omitted judgment supplement, not a new trial.
verification: Primary indexed original and correction checked; full BMJ opening 403.

scope: 32 registered trials supporting claims in 15-country product survey
denominator_type: registered trials cited in surveyed claims

groups.name: No nutrition-industry funding or relevant COI reported

quick: Most registered trials cited for the claims had industry links. That does not mean every product is unsafe.
limitations: Not all formula trials; overlap with first review unresolved. No company-specific counts extracted.

quick: We have not established how many diaper studies were funded by Pampers, Huggies or other companies. A small study found fewer pee cues with disposables, but did not measure when children became independently toilet trained.
limitations: Methods and results may be same cohort; commercial sponsor of 2021 review unresolved. Do not claim a company link without source.

scope: Hydration subset described by 2026 technical reanalysis; inherited Stage 3 extraction
denominator_type: studies in hydration subset, verify primary membership
quick: Most studies in this small hydration subset had industry funding. Four of seven sponsored studies reported a clear benefit, compared with zero of two nonsponsored studies.
limitations: Very small subsets; significance counts not effect sizes or proof that funding caused different results; no pregnancy-specific prevention evidence; recheck original table before use.
verification: Inherited from Stage 3; not independently re-read this pass; research-only example.

quick: The company supplied both lotions in one trial, which did not find reliable stretch-mark prevention.
limitations: In-kind donation is documented in Cochrane trial characterization; total cash support unknown; inherited prior audit.

topic: Pelvic floor therapy after birth injury
quick: A small study supported by public and academic funding found better pelvic floor symptoms after physical therapy.
limitations: Authors declared no conflicts; small injury-specific trial; inherited Stage 3 extraction. Not a universal exercise prescription.
